corpus: Festival receipts 2026 (HYA-417): Maha Shivaratri, Fagu Purnima, Janai Purnima, Teej
method: Publisher day-labels pinned from Hamro Patro BS date pages (festival marks + displayed udaya tithi) and BhaktiBharat daily panchang (tithi transition times). Crawled 2026-11-05. BhaktiBharat live pages cover only a rolling ~2-3 month window, so Feb/Mar tithi timing values are absent; the receipts pin day-labels, udaya labels and convention attribution (the receipt classes the calibration skill accepts).

receipts.receipt: HP marks Maha Shivaratri on Falgun 3 = Feb 15 2026 (Sunday) with udaya tithi Krishna Trayodashi: Chaturdashi began later that day and ran through the midnight ending Feb 15 - the nishita-vyapini rule class ('the timing should be such that Chaturdashi should be till midnight', Dharma Sindhu ch. 5, V.D.N. Rao translation). The udaya convention gives Feb 16; publishers took Feb 15.

HP marks Fagu Purnima (pahadi) on Falgun 18 = Mar 2 2026 with udaya tithi Shukla Chaturdashi: Purnima began mid-day Mar 2, so the hills convention is first-overlap. Terai Holi: Falgun 19 = Mar 3, udaya tithi Shukla Purnima. HP also notes khanda-gras chandra grahan (partial lunar eclipse) on the Terai day - recorded as an eclipse-module receipt (HYA-421).

Purnima began Aug 27 09:24 NPT (BhaktiBharat) and ran to Aug 28 ~10:04, so the first-overlap day is Aug 27; both publishers list Janai Purnima on Bhadra 12 = Aug 28 - the udaya day. A clean divergence receipt: publishers chose udaya-vyapini over purva-viddha.

Shukla Tritiya ran Sep 13 07:24 NPT to Sep 14 07:23 NPT (BhaktiBharat), overlapping both days; HP marks Teej on Bhadra 29 = Sep 14 with udaya tithi Tritiya - the udaya day, not the first-overlap day Sep 13.
